steps.body: Three objects can be put in order by comparing them two at a time: find the longest, then order the rest.
steps.narration: Three objects can be put in order by comparing them two at a time: find the longest, then order the rest.

widget.prompt: Compare this pair fairly, then tap the longer one.
widget.unalignedFeedback: Looks can trick you — line the starting ends up first.
widget.missFeedback: Now the starts are lined up — check the far ends again: the one reaching farther is longer.
widget.successFeedback: The top ribbon reaches farther once both start together — it takes the higher place in the order.

predict.prompt: To order three objects, how many at a time do you compare?
predict.reveal: Comparing pairs is what the eye and the ruler can actually do; the order builds up from those results. Line up all three at once and your eye must judge two far ends in one glance — the middle object is easily misplaced.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g1m order three.
invariants: The manipulated model and the measurement relationship for g1m order three must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Reading a length from appearance or position instead of from same-size units laid end to end.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same measurement?

explanationVariants: Repeat to build the full order.

widget.prompt: The rope is 11 cubes long and the straw is 9 cubes long. How many cubes longer is the rope? Choose the key measurement idea.

commonErrors.feedback: That is the whole length of the rope, not the extra it has beyond the straw.
That is the length of the straw, not the difference between the two.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Re-read the two lengths given, then compare them one step at a time.

hints: Keep the winner and compare again.
Order them from shortest to longest.

steps.body: Ordering is repeated comparing. Each pairwise result narrows the arrangement until only one order fits.
steps.narration: Ordering is repeated comparing. Each pairwise result narrows the arrangement until only one order fits.

widget.prompt: Use this pair to finish the order: align it, then tap the longer object.
widget.unalignedFeedback: The green ribbon starts ahead. Put both starts on the line before ordering the pair.
widget.missFeedback: With matching starts, compare the far ends to place this pair in order.
widget.successFeedback: The orange cord reaches farther, so it belongs above the green ribbon in the order.

explanationVariants: Every pairwise compare needs a fair start.

widget.prompt: Two ribbons lie side by side but one starts 4 units further along. What must you do before deciding which is longer? Show the comparison result.

options.label: Compare the far ends as they lie
options.feedback: With one object shifted 4 units forward, the far ends alone can make the shorter one look longer.

options.label: Pick whichever looks bigger
options.feedback: Appearance is exactly what a shifted starting point distorts; align first, then judge.

options.label: Count the gap between them
options.feedback: The space between two objects describes their positions, not either object's length.

options.label: Line up one end of both first
options.feedback: Correct — a fair comparison starts both objects from the same place, then the far ends decide.

hints: Keep the winner and compare again.
Order them from shortest to longest.

explanationVariants: Longer minus shorter is the gap.
The bigger gap sits further apart in the order.
